sentences.text:
THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY, ORDER  WAS MADE THEREIN AS UNDER:
 -2-  NC: 2024:KHC:45080  CRL.P No. 11508 of 2024 CORAM: HON'BLE MR JUSTICE S VISHWAJITH SHETTY  ORAL ORDER 1.

Accused in Crime No.71/2024 registered by Srirangapatna Rural Police Station, Mandya, for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 504, 506, 307 and 326 of IPC, is before this Court under Section 439 of Cr.P.C.
2. Heard the learned counsel for the parties.
3. FIR in Crime No.71/2024 was registered by Srirangapatna Rural Police Station, Mandya, for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 504, 506 and 307 of IPC, against the petitioner herein on the basis of the first information dated 11.04.2024 received from Roopa B S, who is the wife of petitioner herein.
During the course of investigation, petitioner herein was arrested on 05.06.2024 and subsequently remanded to judicial custody.
Investigation in the case is completed and charge sheet has been filed against the petitioner for the aforesaid offences.
Bail application filed by him before the jurisdictional Sessions Court in Crl.Misc.No.5318/2024 was rejected on 15.10.2024.
Therefore, he is before this Court.
Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that petitioner is an agriculturist without any criminal antecedents.
Petitioner allegedly fought with his wife on the date of incident and thereafter, had assaulted her with an axe causing grievous injuries.
Petitioner is in custody from 06.06.2024.
Investigation in the case is completed and charge sheet has been filed.
Accordingly, he prays to allow the petition.
5. Per contra, learned HCGP has opposed the petition.
He submits that injured has suffered three grievous injuries as a result of assault made by the petitioner.
Petitioner is the husband of injured.
In the event, he is enlarged on bail, he is likely to tamper with the material prosecution witnesses.

Accordingly, he prays to dismiss the petition.
6.
The material on record would go to show that marriage of the injured victim Roopa with the petitioner was solemnized about eight years prior to the alleged date of incident.

From the wedlock,
they have two sons.

In the first information, it is alleged that for the last two years, petitioner was Prasanna vs The State Of Karnataka on 7 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/79655124/
2 suspecting the character of his wife and was harassing her.

sentences.text: Since the petitioner was not earning sufficiently, Roopa started working in NC: 2024:KHC:45080 Senthil Kumar Textiles at Mysuru.
She was daily commuting to Mysuru from Srirangapatna.
On 10.04.2024, petitioner allegedly quarreled with his wife and asked her to stop going to work.
The mother-in-law of Roopa allegedly had pacified both of them and thereafter, all of them had gone to sleep.
At about 02.45 a.m., on the intervening night of 10.04.2024 and 11.04.2024, petitioner allegedly got up and once again started quarrelling with his wife and asked her not to go to work.
When Roopa informed him that on the next day, she will go to the shop to inform her employer, petitioner allegedly got enraged and assaulted her with an axe on her legs.
As a result of the said assault, Roopa had sustained grievous injuries on both legs.
Petitioner was arrested on 06.06.2024.
Investigation in the case is completed and charge sheet has been filed.
It is stated that Roopa has been discharged from the Hospital and her condition is stable.
Petitioner aged about 39 years, is said to be an agriculturist by avocation.
He is in custody for the last more than five months.
Incident had taken place as a result of some dispute between husband and wife.
Under the circumstances, I am of the opinion that the prayer made by the NC: 2024:KHC:45080 petitioner for grant of regular bail needs to be answered affirmatively.

Accordingly, the following order:-
7.
The petition is allowed.
